summary: Describes how link-state and Traffic Engineering information, normally spread by IGP routing protocols, can be collected from a network and shared with outside components using BGP. It is the BGP Link-State (BGP-LS) specification and replaces RFC 7752 and RFC 9029.

eli5.summary: A city map is useful to people outside the city too. This lets routers pass their road map to outside programs through a messaging system called BGP, so those programs can plan routes.

questions: how does bgp-ls carry link-state information
what are bgp-ls producer propagator and consumer
what afi and safi does bgp-ls use
subtitle: How routers hand their view of the network topology and traffic engineering data to outside tools using BGP.

tldr.problem: Path computation elements and ALTO servers need the network topology and traffic engineering data that an IGP distributes, but each IGP area only sees its own part.
tldr.mechanism: BGP-LS carries nodes, links and prefixes as Link-State NLRIs in BGP UPDATE messages, with their properties in a separate BGP-LS Attribute. Both are encoded as Type/Length/Value triplets, under AFI 16388 with SAFI 71, or SAFI 72 for VPN.
tldr.outcome: This document completely replaces RFC 7752 and incorporates RFC 9029, with small changes and clarifications, so it is the current BGP-LS specification.

today: RFC 9552 is a Proposed Standard published in December 2023. It obsoletes RFC 7752 and RFC 9029, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why Link-State Data Goes into BGP
sections.content:
A link-state database or a Traffic Engineering Database (TED) describes only the links and nodes inside one IGP area. Applications such as end-to-end traffic engineering do better with visibility beyond one area or autonomous system.

Two outside consumers are named. A Path Computation Element (PCE, RFC 4655) computes paths that cross more than one TED. Without help, a router can only compute the first area of a multi-area path, which may give suboptimal paths or no path at all. The RFC adds that many implementations make the PCE a passive IGP participant, which may be suboptimal when the network has a lot of churn. An ALTO server (RFC 5693) builds an abstracted topology for network-aware applications and needs both prefix data and TE data.

The solution is a BGP encoding, the BGP-LS mechanism, that collects link-state and TE data and shares it with external components. It applies to physical and virtual links, such as tunnels, and is subject to policy control. A speaker may send the real topology or an abstracted one with virtual, aggregated nodes. It obsoletes RFC 7752 by replacing it, and obsoletes RFC 9029 by incorporating its updates.
sections.eli5: Each neighbourhood knows only its own streets. A route planner needs the whole city map, so the neighbourhoods send their maps to it using the postal system they already have.

sections.title: Producers, Propagators and Consumers
sections.content:
The RFC names three roles for the BGP implementation. A BGP-LS Producer originates link-state information into BGP, usually from its IGP, and may also add local information from other sources. A BGP-LS Propagator processes BGP-LS UPDATE messages and runs the BGP Decision Process to decide what to pass on, as a route reflector would. A BGP-LS Consumer is an application, not a BGP speaker, that receives the information.

The roles are not mutually exclusive, so one speaker can produce some information and propagate other information. The link from a speaker to a consumer MUST be unidirectional: a consumer MUST NOT be able to send information to a speaker for origination into BGP-LS. The interface between BGP and the consumer is outside the scope of the RFC.
sections.eli5: Some routers write down what they see, some pass notes along, and some outside programs only read them. The readers are not allowed to write anything back.

sections.title: TLV Format and Ordering Rules
sections.content:
Everything in the Link-State NLRI and in the BGP-LS Attribute is encoded as Type/Length/Value triplets. The Type and Length fields are 16 bits each, the Length counts the value in octets, and TLVs are not padded to 4-octet alignment.

Unknown and unsupported TLV types MUST be preserved and propagated, and unknown or unexpected TLVs MUST NOT make the NLRI or the attribute malformed. That lets new TLVs spread through route reflectors that do not yet understand them.

To compare NLRIs, the TLVs inside an NLRI MUST be in ascending order by type, and TLVs of the same type MUST be ordered by length and then by value, treated as opaque bytes. An NLRI that breaks this ordering MUST be considered malformed by a Propagator. Inside the BGP-LS Attribute, TLVs SHOULD be in ascending order but unordered ones are not malformed.
sections.eli5: Every piece of information is a labelled box saying what it is, how big it is, and what is inside. A reader that does not know a label still passes the box on untouched.

sections.title: The Link-State NLRI
sections.content:
Link-state data travels in BGP UPDATE messages in two parts: NLRI inside the MP_REACH_NLRI and MP_UNREACH_NLRI attributes, describing node, link or prefix objects, and the BGP-LS Attribute (path attribute value 29), an optional, non-transitive attribute carrying their properties. Non-VPN data uses AFI 16388 with SAFI 71, and VPN data uses SAFI 72, which adds an 8-octet Route Distinguisher. Speakers MUST negotiate the capability using multiprotocol BGP before exchanging it.

Four NLRI types are defined: Node, Link, IPv4 Topology Prefix and IPv6 Topology Prefix. Unknown NLRI types MUST be handled as opaque objects and preserved and propagated. Each NLRI starts with a one-octet Protocol-ID naming the source (IS-IS Level 1 or 2, OSPFv2, OSPFv3, Direct or Static configuration) and an 8-octet Identifier.

The Identifier carries the BGP-LS Instance-ID, which tells apart independent IGP routing domains. Instance-ID 0 is RECOMMENDED when there is a single instance. The operator MUST use the same Instance-ID on all Producers in one IGP domain, and unique ones for different domains. When a TLV in an NLRI is added, removed or changed, the Producer MUST withdraw the old NLRI.
sections.eli5: Each message says whether it describes a router, a connection between two routers, or an address range. It also says which routing system it came from, so the reader can keep different networks apart.

sections.title: Descriptors and Attributes
sections.content:
The NLRI holds descriptors, which identify the object, and the BGP-LS Attribute holds attributes, which describe it. A Local Node Descriptors TLV (type 256) is mandatory in all three NLRI kinds. A Link NLRI also carries a Remote Node Descriptors TLV (type 257). Node descriptor sub-TLVs include the Autonomous System (512), the OSPF Area-ID (514) and the IGP Router-ID (515). The BGP-LS Identifier (513) is deprecated in this document.

A link is described as a unidirectional half-link. To describe one link, the two anchor routers each advertise one Link NLRI, and a link is not complete or available unless both halves are present, much like the IGP two-way connectivity check. Link descriptors include the interface and neighbor addresses or the local and remote identifiers, and a Multi-Topology Identifier (263) when the link is in a non-default topology. IPv6 or IPv4 link-local addresses MUST NOT be used as link descriptors.

Prefix descriptors include an OSPF Route Type (264) and the mandatory IP Reachability Information (265). The attributes cover node data such as flag bits, name and TE Router-IDs, link data such as maximum and unreserved bandwidth, TE default metric, IGP metric and Shared Risk Link Groups, and prefix data such as IGP flags, route tags and prefix metric. Vendors may use a reserved private-use range, where a 4-octet Enterprise Code comes first.
sections.eli5: The first part of a note says exactly which router, road or address range it is about. The second part says things like how wide the road is and how long it takes to drive.

sections.title: Producing, Sizing and Aggregating
sections.content:
The BGP-LS information is derived from the IGP database, but it is not a verbatim copy. It leaves out LSA or LSP sequence numbers, purged or aged-out entries, and invalid or malformed content, and some information such as OSPF virtual links.

Size matters. BGP normally limits a message to 4096 octets, and the RFC RECOMMENDS support for the extended message size of RFC 8654. A Producer MUST NOT build an UPDATE for a single Link-State NLRI that crosses the limit, and a Propagator that exceeds it MUST treat the BGP-LS Attribute as malformed and apply Attribute Discard.

Unreachable nodes need care. If a Producer keeps advertising objects learned from stale LSAs, a consumer may get stale or inaccurate topology, for example miss that an area is partitioned. A Producer SHOULD withdraw all objects from an IGP node that has become unreachable, and MUST re-advertise them once the node is reachable again.

Finally, advertising every link of the global Internet is neither desirable for scaling nor for privacy, so an ASBR may advertise an aggregate link between a non-adjacent pair of nodes. Whether to expose specific or aggregated links is the operator's policy choice.
sections.eli5: The map that gets sent is a tidied-up copy, not a photocopy of every scribble. If a road is reported closed, the sender takes it off the map, and puts it back when it opens.

sections.title: Running BGP-LS in a Network
sections.content:
Existing BGP operational procedures apply. BGP-LS data is application-level information and has no immediate effect on the forwarding state computed by BGP, so churn has a different impact than ordinary updates. Distribution SHOULD be handled by dedicated route reflectors, or by separate BGP instances or sessions.

Operators are RECOMMENDED to enable two or more Producers in each IGP flooding domain, to use at least a pair of route reflectors, and to ensure that consumers receive the topology from at least two speakers. By default the Link-State NLRI capability is off for all neighbors and the maximum rate of advertisements and withdrawals is 200 updates per second. Because the extension is activated only after capability negotiation and can be turned on per peer, it can be rolled out gradually.
sections.eli5: Use more than one reporter so that one sick reporter does not leave the map blank. Start with the feature off and switch it on one neighbour at a time.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC says the mechanism does not affect the BGP security model and points to the BGP security discussions in RFC 4271. Operators should make sure a speaker does not accept UPDATE messages from a peer that is only meant to give information to a consumer.

Errors or tampering in the link-state data, such as wrong information, wrong TLV ordering or inconsistent origination from several Producers, can make consumer applications malfunction. These are not new BGP risks, but the impact falls on consumers rather than on BGP routing.

Exporting link-state and TE data may also expose commercially sensitive information about the network. BGP peerings require configuration, so the operator is responsible for configuring only trusted speakers to receive it.
sections.eli5: A wrong map can send the delivery trucks the wrong way, and a map of your roads is private. So you only share it with people you have chosen to trust.
